svg.title: Layered Logic Mirror — Settings → Wi-Fi screen wireframe
svg.desc: Lo-fi wireframe of the React Native Settings screen's Wi-Fi section in the Layered Logic Mirror app. Shows the resting state (mirror name field, current network with IP, saved-networks list with active/forget/connect controls, add-network button, firmware update check) with 6 numbered callouts pairing each UI decision to its source rationale doc. A 4-thumbnail strip below documents the loading, switching, confirm-forget, and list-full alternate states. Phone proportions match Pixel 9 (360x800 dp, 9:20 ratio). Brand indigo (#3214FF) marks the active/primary affordances; everything else is grayscale lo-fi.
svg.text: Layered Logic Mirror · App/v1 · Mobile (React Native, Pixel 9)
Shown when multiple mirrors are on one network.
Empty falls back to the hardware ID.
Adding a network saves it for later — the mirror
won't switch to it until the current network
Surface the IP, not just the SSID
Webapp hid IP inside its mDNS hostname URL. With multi-network,
"which IP did it land on?" matters more — especially across /24s.
Settings exposes both so cross-subnet lookups don't need ARP
is_active comes from firmware, not the app's locally-cached "last
connected SSID". Covers the cross-client case (webapp adds or
switches while RN app is open). Re-fetched on state.wifi_ssid
change so the optimistic-clear settles to truth.
Added during hardware test of LL-046 step 6. "No auto-SoftAP"
leaves the user stuck if they provision a bad 2nd network and
forget the 1st. Connect op posts LL_EV_WIFI_REQUEST_SWITCH so
the STA teardown happens AFTER the response flushes.
Departure from iOS's passive "stay connected until natural
disconnect" pattern. Confirm dialog gates the destructive action;
on confirm, device drops the connection NOW. Non-active rows
Add-network form saves the entry; doesn't switch. Helper text
below the button explicitly states this so the user knows what
to expect. New entry sits in the saved list; the connection state
machine picks it up automatically when the current network drops.
Realistic personal-use ceiling: home, work, parents, travel
hotspot. 5th add returns wifi_list_full — the user picks what to
evict rather than the firmware deciding for them.
Bug-driven decisions in the callouts above protect against specific failure states. Each thumbnail shows the surface in that state.
on tap; brand banner + haptic confirm

Modal gates Forget on the active
prompt — same UX norm as iOS for
User picks what to evict — firmware
never decides. Easy to bump N_MAX
later; hard to lower without migration.
